items.title: 9.5 Ethical, Legal, and Environmental Impacts of Computing

source_refs.note: Topic 9.5 as printed (PDF 135-137, printed 131-133) with its Do You Know, Class Activity and Tidbit; every printed sub-heading as a heading. No book figure.

blocks.text: Computing affects many aspects of daily life. Technology can have ethical or unethical effects, legal or illegal consequences, and can impact the environment. Ethical use involves making fair and responsible choices when using digital tools. Legal use follows the laws related to technology. Environmental impact includes energy consumption, electronic waste, and other effects on nature. Awareness of these impacts helps make informed and responsible decisions when using computing resources.
Ethical Use of Technology

Ethical use of technology involves acting responsibly and avoiding harm through digital actions. This includes respecting privacy, fairness, and proper handling of information. Following ethical guidelines helps maintain trust and safety online. Decisions in technology should consider the potential effects on people, organizations, and society. Responsible use of digital tools supports a safe and fair digital environment.

blocks.title: Do You Know?
blocks.text: Copying online content without permission can violate both copyright laws and digital ethics
Respecting Intellectual Property and Data Ownership

Intellectual property refers to creative work such as software, music, or writing. Data ownership refers to the right to control personal information. Respecting these rights means avoiding copying, sharing, or using work without permission. Personal and sensitive information should be protected and not misused. Legal and ethical respect for intellectual property and data encourages fairness and protects creators and users.
Understanding Consequences of Unethical Digital Behavior

Unethical digital behavior can include hacking, spreading false information, or cyberbullying. Such actions can cause harm, damage reputations, and lead to legal consequences. Even small actions online may have significant effects. Understanding the outcomes of unethical behavior encourages responsible digital conduct. Maintaining ethical standards ensures a safer and more trustworthy online environment.
Legal Aspects and Data Privacy Laws

Legal aspects of computing refer to the rules and regulations that govern the use of technology and digital information. Cybercrime refers to illegal activities carried out using computers, networks, or the internet, such as hacking, identity theft, and online fraud. These laws protect individuals, organizations, and society from misuse of data and technology. Data privacy laws ensure that personal and sensitive information is collected, stored, and shared responsibly. Understanding these laws helps prevent legal issues and promotes safe digital practices. Compliance with legal frameworks also encourages trust in online systems and services.
Overview of International Frameworks (e.g., GDPR)

The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) is a law in the European Union that protects personal data. It sets rules on how organizations collect, store, and use data. GDPR requires transparency, consent, and the right to access or delete personal information. Many countries and companies follow similar standards to ensure data privacy globally. These frameworks aim to prevent misuse of personal information and promote accountability.
Cybercrime Laws and Data Protection Policies in Pakistan

Pakistan has laws to prevent cybercrime and protect digital information. The Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (PECA) 2016 is the main law in Pakistan that deals with cybercrime. It aims to protect individuals, organizations, and the state from illegal activities carried out using computers, mobile devices, and the internet. These laws cover hacking, identity theft, online fraud, and unauthorized access to data. Organizations are required to follow data protection policies to secure sensitive information. Legal penalties exist for violating cybercrime and data privacy laws. Following these regulations helps maintain security and trust in digital systems within the country.

Environmental and Social Impacts

Computing affects the environment and society in many ways. Technology can consume energy, produce electronic waste, and contribute to pollution. At the same time, technology influences social behavior, communication, and culture. Understanding environmental and social impacts helps promote responsible use of digital tools. Sustainable practices and awareness of societal effects are important for balancing technology with nature and communities.
E-waste Management and Sustainable Computing

Electronic waste (e-waste) is created when devices are discarded or replaced. Improper disposal of e-waste can harm the environment and human health. Sustainable computing includes recycling, reusing, and reducing electronic devices responsibly. Energy-efficient devices and environmentally friendly practices reduce the negative impact of technology. Proper e-waste management ensures resources are preserved and pollution is minimized.

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text: Recycling, reusing, and energy-efficient devices reduce environmental harm.
The Role of Technology in Cultural and Societal Change

Technology changes how people communicate, work, and access information. Social media, digital learning, and online services influence culture and daily life. Technology can improve education, healthcare, and business efficiency. However, it can also create challenges such as digital divide or loss of privacy. Understanding these social impacts encourages thoughtful and responsible use of technology in communities.
